title: Miscellaneous
text:
This page is for things that don’t quite fit into “formal research” but are still part of what I care about and what I’m experimenting with.



Right now, I’m:

Wrapping up projects on mutual intelligibility benchmarks and visual reasoning.
Cleaning up codebases so they are easier to reproduce and open-source.
Slowly rebuilding my personal website and trying to write more consistently.





A non-exhaustive list of things I like thinking about or doing when I’m not debugging training loops:

Fitness & health – trying to get leaner and keep a sustainable routine around home workouts and cardio.
Day trading & markets – learning how markets work, experimenting with small positions, and figuring out how to not be stupid with money.
Tooling & workflows – shells, dotfiles, terminals, and anything that makes working on code less painful.





Occasionally I run small side experiments that may or may not go anywhere:

Playing with agentic systems that combine tools, memory, and “mood” for more persistent AI characters.
Building personal finance / expense tracking tools (e.g., parsing mobile money SMS for automatic budgeting).
Sketching ideas for Amharic-first LLMs, starting from data collection and evaluation strategies.

If any of these resonate with you, feel free to reach out — I’m always open to collaborating on interesting side projects.

title: Tewodros Idris
text:
GitHub · LinkedIn · Google Scholar · Email
I’m a machine learning engineer and researcher working on NLP and multimodal systems, with a particular focus on low-resource languages, mutual intelligibility in language models, and vision–language reasoning.
Right now, I’m a Research Associate at CMU-Africa, where I spend most of my time thinking about: - How language models generalize across related languages - How to make models reason better using images, diagrams, and structured HTML - How to build practical systems (RAG, ASR, agentic pipelines) that actually get used
Previously, I worked as a Protocol Engineer at NuNet, building distributed systems and GPU job orchestration on decentralized infrastructure.

title: Tewodros Idris
text:
Research

Mutual intelligibility in language models
I’m working on using embedding-space structure to study how models handle languages they were never trained on. Roughly:

Use multilingual encoders and FLORES+/other benchmarks

Compare distances and similarities between languages in embedding space

Study how this correlates with typological distance and zero-shot performance

The long-term goal is to better understand which parts of a corpus actually matter for cross-lingual transfer, especially for low-resource African languages.


Self-Imagine: visual and HTML-based reasoning
In another line of work, I’m exploring how models can “self-generate” diagrams, images, or HTML layouts to help them reason better on math and symbolic tasks.
This involves:

Generating images/HTML for datasets like GSM8K, SVAMP, ASDiv

Evaluating answer self-consistency and image/HTML quality

Analyzing which visual/structural representations help models the most

title: Tewodros Idris
text:
Selected projects & competitions

Specializing LLMs for Telecom Networks (Zindi)
Built a retrieval-augmented QA system for telecom multiple-choice questions using ColBERT-style dense retrieval and domain documents. This work led to a Zindi competition win and an accompanying arXiv paper:
Zindi telecom RAG paper
Low-resource ASR and speech tech
Worked on Amharic and Swahili ASR in collaboration with WAVLab at CMU Pittsburgh, extending toolkits and exploring data collection strategies when labeled data is scarce.
Generative AI: controllable music generation
Course project using MusicGen + textual inversion to learn token embeddings corresponding to musical “styles” and compose them at inference time for more controllable music generation.
Crisis & clinical ML challenges
Participated in multiple Zindi/Kaggle challenges around crisis response, healthcare decision support, time-series forecasting, and geospatial ML.

title: Rebooting the site
text:
What I’ll write about
I expect posts here to be a mix of:

Research notes

mutual intelligibility in language models

low-resource languages (especially African languages)

vision–language reasoning, HTML diagrams, and self-consistency

Engineering / tooling

training and evaluating models on HPC clusters

RAG and agentic systems for real problems (not just toy demos)

debugging, logging, and experiment tracking workflows

Life / process

navigating grad school and research from Africa

competitions (Zindi, Kaggle) and what I learned from them

fitness, money, and trying to build a sustainable routine around all of this


I don’t plan to make every post polished or “paper-like”. Some will just be structured notes or partial experiments that I want to document publicly.

title: Rebooting the site
text:
If you’re reading this
The site is still very much a work in progress — layout, styling, and content will all evolve.
For now, I mainly wanted the basics working:

index.qmd as an About page

this blog post to confirm Quarto is wired correctly

a misc page for everything that doesn’t fit anywhere else

If you spot something broken or want to discuss anything I write here, feel free to open an issue on GitHub or reach out directly.
